characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-RB, Cu target, operated at 40 kV and 150 mA
characterization_methods.key_findings: No κ-carbide peaks are present in the 1000 °C specimen (κ reflections only for 700, 800, 850 °C); lattice parameters α = 2.89–2.91 Å, γ = 3.65–3.67 Å, κ = 3.76–3.79 Å.
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and determination of phase volume fractions by the direct comparison method

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss AxioCam MRc5; specimens mechanically polished and etched in 8% Nital
characterization_methods.key_findings: The banded structure persists at 1000 °C but becomes less contiguous and coarser; α and γ grains appear coarser and more equiaxed.
characterization_methods.purpose: Observation of the banded microstructure and phase distribution (RD–ND and RD–TD sections)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Quanta 450 operated at an acceleration voltage of 20 kV, equipped with EDS
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 1000 °C matrix is free of resolvable κ-carbide; bright boundary κ films exist along boundaries of large α grains (Fig. 10(b)).
characterization_methods.purpose: Examination of microstructure, boundary κ-carbide and phase chemical composition
characterization_methods.technique: Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with energy dispersive spectrometry (EDS)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2100 operated at an acceleration voltage of 200 kV; thin foils prepared by twin-jet polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol at -30 °C and 30 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: TEM analysis indicates no obvious superlattice spots in the SADPs of α or γ in all annealed specimens, so atomic ordering is not expected during 700–1200 °C annealing for 1 h.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identification of phases and orientation relationships (performed for specimens annealed at 700, 800, 1100 and 1200 °C; not reported specifically for 1000 °C)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Grain sizes of the annealed specimens (900–1200 °C) increase with temperature; data plotted in Fig. 9.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measurement of average grain sizes of α1, α2 and γ as a function of annealing temperature
characterization_methods.technique: Grain size measurement from SEM micrographs

characterization_methods.key_findings: 1000 °C/1 h specimen: UTS 763 MPa, YS 557 MPa, ultimate elongation 16.2%, strength–ductility product 12 GPa%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 3 × 10^-4 s^-1, gage length 50 mm, gage width 12.5 mm, tensile axis parallel to RD
characterization_methods.purpose: Measurement of ultimate strength, yield strength and ultimate elongation of the annealed specimens

characterization_methods.key_findings: Density of the present steel ≈ 6.80 g/cm3, about 13% lower than pure Fe.

Fracture of the 1000 °C specimen is predominant by a mixture of ductile fracture of γ and quasi-cleavage fracture of α, with large banding-related secondary cracks; the ductile fracture area is smaller/less apparent than at 900 °C.
characterization_methods.purpose: Investigation of the fracture mode of the tensile specimens

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium phase fractions of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ) calculated for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C composition at temperatures above 550 °C
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The Thermo-Calc κ-carbide dissolution temperature (~823 °C) is lower than the experimentally measured 850–900 °C, attributed to the steel not being in equilibrium and to the difference between atomic-fraction (calculated) and volume-fraction (XRD-measured) fractions.

interfaces.interface_notes: The κ-carbide present along α/α boundaries in the 1000 °C specimen cannot be detected by XRD, probably because its fraction is too small (b0033). The dissolving sequence: κ at/near α/γ boundaries dissolves first, κ along α/α boundaries of large grains dissolves last (b0048).
interfaces.phase_evolution: At 1000 °C the intragranular κ-carbide has dissolved into the α and γ matrices (κ dissolution temperature between 850 and 900 °C), so no matrix κ-carbide is resolvable (Fig. 6(f)); the boundary κ-carbide observed along some α/α boundaries is believed to form during quenching when the annealing temperature exceeds the κ dissolution temperature. γ fraction reaches a maximum (~63%) around 1000 °C, and α and γ grains coarsen strongly above 900 °C.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 20 kg ingot of a Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting method.
The ingot was heated to 1200 °C and then forged to forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h before hot rolling.
The forging blank was hot-rolled to a plate of 3 mm thickness, with the finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C (parent hot-rolled process proc_hr).
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: hot-rolled to plate of 3 mm thickness

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After rolling the plate was water quenched to about 300 °C (Fig. 1: 'water cooled' to 300 °C then 'air cooled').
The hot-rolled plate was annealed at 1000 °C for 1 h (this is the defining step of the sample proc_1000c-1h-wq; annealing range 700–1200 °C for 1 h in Fig. 1).
The 1000 °C/1 h anneal was followed by water quenching.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile axis parallel to the rolling direction
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage length 50 mm, gage width 12.5 mm

elongation.direction: rolling direction (tensile axis parallel to RD)

strain_hardening_rate: For the 1000 °C specimen (with no obvious κ-carbide in the α or γ matrix) the work hardening rate is lower than that of the 700/800/850 °C specimens when true strain is less than about 5%; the work hardening rate curve was calculated from the yielding period.
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–engineering strain (Fig. 15(a)) and true stress–true strain (Fig. 15(b)) curves are reported for the 1000 °C, 1 h specimen; the 1000 °C curve lies below the lower-temperature curves.

ultimate_tensile_strength.direction: rolling direction (tensile axis parallel to RD)

yield_strength.direction: rolling direction (tensile axis parallel to RD)

phases_present.morphology: coarse continuous banded-shape grains (α2) plus finer α grains distributed among γ grains (α1)
phases_present.volume_fraction: ≈0.4 (approximate, read from Fig. 14 for the 900–1200 °C range)

phases_present.morphology: boundary films along α/α boundaries of some large α grains, formed during quenching
phases_present.volume_fraction: very small; not detectable by XRD at 900–1200 °C

precipitates.distribution: along some large α grains / α/α boundaries

structures.overall_structure: Banded duplex α + γ microstructure with coarse grains and a residual banded ferrite structure; matrix κ-carbide has dissolved at 1000 °C but small boundary κ-carbide forms during quenching along some α/α boundaries of large α grains.

unmapped_findings: Fracture of the 1000 °C/1 h specimen (Fig. 17(e),(f)) is predominately a mixture of ductile fracture of the γ phase and quasi-cleavage fracture of the α phase, with large banding-related secondary cracks; the ductile fracture area in the 1000 °C specimen is less obvious/less apparent than in the 900 °C specimen. The effect of boundary κ-carbide along large α grains could not be resolved from the fractographs.
No TRIP or TWIP phenomenon was found during the tensile test of the annealed specimens, according to post-deformation TEM examination (b0040).

TEM analysis indicates that no obvious superlattice spots are seen in the SADPs of α or γ in all the annealed specimens, so atomic ordering in α or γ is not expected during annealing at 700–1200 °C for 1 h; ordering may occur during quenching but the time is too short for it to develop (b0033).

Alloy-level comparative performance (Table 2, for the present Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel using its optimum 900 °C/1 h properties, NOT this 1000 °C sample): present steel 855 MPa UTS / 651 MPa YS / 36.6% elongation / 31 GPa% product (phase γ + α (40%) + boundary κ), versus Fe–28Mn–10Al–1.0C 873/572/γ/98.9/86; Fe–20Mn–9Al–0.6C 830/535/γ+α(34%)/45.6/38; Fe–18Mn–10Al–1.2C 875/702/γ+κ/77.4/68; Fe–18Mn–10Al–0.8C 966/801/γ+κ+α(24%)/44/43; Fe–12Mn–8.0Al–0.8C 920/670/γ+κ+α(21%)/46.4/43. The present steel has the lowest elongation and lowest strength–ductility product of the set.

For the 1000 °C specimen the γ fraction is the maximum for this steel (~63%) and α and γ grains grow rapidly above 900 °C; because phase fractions change only in the narrow 57–63% γ range between 900 and 1200 °C, the grain size (Hall–Petch) rather than phase fraction controls the tensile properties in that range (b0033, b0053, b0067, b0079).
